beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It was late on the night before he died. The supper was over, the songs were sung, and Jesus led his friends out of the city, down across the valley, and up into a quiet grove of olive trees called Gethsemane. He had come here often. But this night was not like the others.

timing.text: It was late on the night before he died.
The supper was over, the songs were sung, and Jesus led his friends out of the city, down across the valley, and up into a quiet grove of olive trees called Gethsemane.
He had come here often.
But this night was not like the others.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: At the edge of the garden he stopped, and asked most of them to sit and wait while he went ahead to pray. He told them gently to pray as well, so that what was coming would not overtake them. Then he went deeper into the trees.

timing.text: At the edge of the garden he stopped, and asked most of them to sit and wait while he went ahead to pray.

Then he went deeper into the trees.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He took only three with him — Peter, James, and John, the ones who had been closest to him. And as he walked, something began to break over him: a weight none of them had ever seen him carry. He was sorrowful, and deeply troubled.

timing.text: He took only three with him — Peter, James, and John, the ones who had been closest to him.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me.

timing.text: My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He did not hide it from them. He told them plainly how heavy his heart was — heavy enough, he said, to crush the life out of him — and he asked them simply to stay near, and stay awake, while he prayed. He did not want to be alone.

timing.text: He did not hide it from them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then he went on a little further by himself, about as far as a man can throw a stone, and he sank down onto the ground among the roots and the rocks. Everything that was coming, all of it, he carried to his Father in prayer.

timing.text: Then he went on a little further by himself, about as far as a man can throw a stone, and he sank down onto the ground among the roots and the rocks.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.

timing.text: Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He asked, honestly, if there were any other way — if this cup of suffering could pass from him, let it pass. But even in his agony he did not stop there. Whatever his Father wanted, that was what he wanted more. Not his own will, he prayed, but his Father's.

timing.text: He asked, honestly, if there were any other way — if this cup of suffering could pass from him, let it pass.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This was no calm, quiet moment. Luke, who was a physician, tells us that as he prayed in that anguish, his sweat fell like great drops of blood to the ground. The suffering was real, and he felt every ounce of it. And still he stayed, and still he prayed.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And heaven did not leave him there alone. An angel came to him out of the darkness and strengthened him. God's answer, in that hour, was not to take the pain away. It was to come near, and hold him up, and give him what he needed to go on. He was not abandoned.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: When he rose and came back to his three friends, he found them fast asleep. Not from carelessness — Luke says they were sleeping for sorrow. Their own grief had worn them out. He had asked them to watch with him, and they could not.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

timing.text: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He woke them, but he did not scold them. He understood exactly what they were made of. Their hearts longed to be faithful; their tired bodies simply gave out. He knew the difference, and he was tender with them even now, on the worst night of his life.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He went back and prayed again, and a third time, the very same words, until his heart was fully settled. The struggle was over. He had looked straight at everything that was coming, and he had said yes to his Father anyway. He rose from that place resolved.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that doth betray me.

timing.text: Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that doth betray me.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Across the valley, torches were already winding up the hill — the men who had come to arrest him. He did not run, and he did not hide. He woke his friends, and he walked out to meet it. Everything he had just wrestled with in the dark, he now carried toward the cross. He did it on purpose. He did it for us.

card.text: On the hardest night of his life, Jesus asked his Father for another way — and then trusted him with the answer. He faced that night so that you would never have to face your darkest one alone. Where is he asking you to trust him, even now?
